 W.P.(CRL) 810/2023 1.

This is a petition seeking quashing of the FIR No. 412/2022 dated 08.07.2022 registered at PS Mehrauli under Section 498A/406/34 IPC.
2.
During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties have arrived at a settlement dated 17.01.2023, wherein a total sum of Rs. 4.5 lakhs was to be paid to the respondent No.2 by the petitioner.
A sum of Rs. 2.5 lakhs has already been paid to the respondent No.2 and balance sum of Rs. 2 lakhs is being paid today in Court vide DD No. 574794 dated 20.03.2023 drawn on Punjab National Bank.
3. The petitioners are present in Court and have been identified by Ms. Vinita Sharma, learned counsel.
4. The respondent No.2 is also present in Court and has been identified by Mr. Amar Nath, learned counsel and ASI Vinod, PS Mehrauli.

sentences.text: The parties state that they have arrived at the above said settlement out of their own free will and without any undue influence, threat, pressure or coercion.
6. The respondent No.2 has no objection if the present FIR No. 412/2022 is quashed.
7. There are two minor children born out of the wedlock who, as of today, are in the care and custody of the respondent No.2 but they shall now onwards be in the care and custody of the petitioner.

8. Even though the MoU says that the respondent No.2 shall not be meeting the children, the respondent No.2 who is present in Court today, states that it was an inadvertent error and she wants to meet the children.
9. The petitioner who is present in Court states that respondent No.2 shall have unhindered visitation rights to meet her children as and when she wants.
In case the respondent No.2 wishes to meet the children, she will inform the petitioner one day earlier regarding the same.
The respondent No.2 shall ensure that the educational curriculum of the children is not affected in any way by her visitation.
10. The petitioner ensures that the meeting and visitation takes place in a smooth, friendly and congenial environment.

11. With these directions and taking the statements of the petitioner and respondent No.2 on record,
the FIR No. 412/2022 dated 08.07.2022 registered at PS Mehrauli under Section 498A/406/34 IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are hereby quashed.
12. The petition is disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
JASMEET SINGH, J MARCH 21, 2023 /
